chapter: Lil, Oliver and the Hot Five
title: Never meeting Lil; Chicago in 1929 and Armstrong on the road
summary: Alcorn never met Lil Armstrong; he was in Chicago in 1929 while Louis was already east, and comments on Louis always traveling.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: Yeah. Did you ever meet his wife, Lil, Lil Harden?
You know, I never did meet Lil. Yeah. Because when I was in, uh, around Chicago, the little name of it, left way from around there, I went to Chicago in 29. I don't know where Lil had gone.
You went to Chicago in 1929. 29. Yeah. I lived, I lived with that for a short time, my mother then.

Mm-hmm. And, uh, Louis was gone. Louis was gone to New York. Uh-huh. All over all the places. I never didn't get a chance to see Louis in, in Chicago, because he had gone east. Mm-hmm. And worked around on the road, because he was always a man that went on the road all the time.

He was saying, he traveled, always traveled. I never saw another man. No man in music ever traveled with his book. He must have loved it, though. Well, he had, uh, I guess he did love it, because everything he, anytime he put on the show, you could see he was very much pleased with what he was doing. Yeah. A guy, it could be angry, breaking the back, but when he come on that stage, full of smiles, you know, just a natural.
